examples.en: With supermarkets getting bigger, small shops have had a hard time.

examples.ko: 자동차의 대형화 추세 때문에 주차장이 좁게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Because cars are getting bigger, parking lots feel cramped.

examples.ko: 대형화가 항상 좋은 건 아니라는 의견도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say that getting bigger isn't always a good thing.

examples.ko: 회사는 사업 대형화를 목표로 직원을 늘리고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is hiring more staff with the goal of expanding its business.
As they got bigger, the prices went up a lot too.

examples.ko: 농장의 대형화는 환경 문제로 이어지기도 해요.
examples.en: Making farms larger can also lead to environmental problems.

explain: '대형'(큰 것)에 '-화'가 붙어서 작던 것이 점점 커지는 변화를 말할 때 써요. 반대로 작게 만드는 것은 '소형화'예요. 뉴스에서는 '병원의 대형화', '기업 대형화'처럼 쓰고, '대형화하다'로도 말해요.

phrases.en: These days hospitals are getting larger and larger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대형화' 뒤에 '-하다'를 붙여 스스로 커진다는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -하다 describes something growing larger on its own.

phrases.en: As the store was enlarged, the customers increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-되다'는 어떤 영향으로 커지게 되었다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -되다 suggests something has been made larger by outside forces.

phrases.en: The enlargement of companies also affects jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 명사로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common noun phrase in news and writing.

explain_en: '대형' (large) plus '-화' describes a change in which something gets bigger and bigger. The opposite is '소형화' (making smaller). In the news you see it in phrases like '병원의 대형화' and '기업 대형화', and it can also be used as '대형화하다'.

en: to be tiny; to be fine; to be minute

examples.en: The camera shook slightly, so the photo is blurry.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 아주 미세한 소리도 잡아내요.
examples.en: This machine picks up even very faint sounds.
The difference between the two products is too subtle.
Just because it's tiny doesn't mean you can ignore it.
The finer it is, the harder it is to check by eye.
The change in taste was so subtle that nobody noticed.

explain: '작다'는 크기가 작을 때 쓰고, '미세하다'는 눈에 거의 안 보이거나 차이가 거의 없을 때 써요. '미세한 차이', '미세하게 떨리다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 '미세먼지'의 '미세'가 바로 이 말이에요.

phrases.example: 두 색 사이에 미세한 차이가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a tiny difference between the two colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 느끼기 어려운 아주 작은 차이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a difference so small it is hard to notice.

phrases.en: My hands tremble slightly because I'm nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 잘 안 보일 만큼 조금 떨릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something shakes so little it is barely visible.

phrases.example: 먼지 입자가 너무 미세해서 눈에 안 보여요.
phrases.en: The dust particles are so fine that you can't see them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미세하다'를 해요체로 말한 형태로, 아주 작고 가는 것을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, describing something extremely small and fine.

explain_en: So small it is hard to see; written or technical (미세한 먼지) '작다' is for plain smallness; 미세하다 is for things almost too small to see or differences almost too small to notice. It usually modifies something, as in '미세한 차이' (a subtle difference) or '미세하게 떨리다' (to tremble slightly). The '미세' in the news word 미세먼지 (fine dust) is this word.

t90.ax: This machine picks up even very faint sounds.

examples.en: This gold ring has high purity.
It says the water is 99 percent pure.
I went to the shop to check the purity of the gold.

examples.ko: 순도 차이 때문에 가격이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: The price differs a lot because of the difference in purity.
In the lab, they only use high-purity materials.

examples.ko: 이 소금은 순도를 높이는 과정을 거쳐요.
examples.en: This salt goes through a process that raises its purity.

explain: 금, 물, 소금, 화학 재료처럼 다른 것이 섞이지 않은 정도를 말할 때 써요. '순도가 높다/낮다/높이다'로 쓰고, 퍼센트 같은 숫자와 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요. '품질'은 전체적인 좋고 나쁨이고, '순도'는 불순물이 적은 정도예요.

phrases.example: 이 소금은 순도가 낮아서 다른 맛이 나요.
phrases.en: This salt has low purity, so it tastes a bit off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순도가 높다'의 반대로, 다른 것이 많이 섞여 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 순도가 높다; it means a lot of other things are mixed in.

phrases.example: 공장에서는 물의 순도를 높이는 작업을 해요.
phrases.en: The factory does work to raise the purity of the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불순물을 없애서 더 깨끗하게 만든다는 뜻으로, 과학이나 산업 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to remove impurities and make something purer; common in science and industry.

phrases.example: 순도 높은 금은 색이 아주 진해요.
phrases.en: High-purity gold has a very deep color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 '순도 높은 금', '순도 높은 물'처럼 물건을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a material, as in 'high-purity gold' or 'high-purity water'.

explain_en: It is used for things like gold, water, salt and chemicals, to say how free they are of other substances. Use it as '순도가 높다/낮다/높이다', often with numbers such as percentages. '품질' is overall quality, while '순도' is specifically how few impurities there are.

examples.ko: 이 제품이 다른 것보다 월등히 좋아요.
examples.en: This product is far better than the others.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 실력이 월등히 뛰어나서 상대가 없어요.
examples.en: That player's skill is so far above the rest that no one can match him.
This year, sales have increased far beyond last year's.

examples.ko: 두 후보의 점수 차이가 월등히 커졌어요.
examples.en: The score gap between the two candidates grew significantly.

examples.ko: 우리 반에서 월등히 키가 큰 아이가 있어요.
examples.en: There's a child in our class who is far taller than the rest.

examples.ko: 형은 영어를 월등히 잘해서 통역도 도와줘요.
examples.en: My older brother is so much better at English that he even helps with interpreting.

explain: '훨씬'과 비슷하지만 다른 것들과 비교해서 한참 앞서거나 뛰어나다는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '좋다, 뛰어나다, 앞서다, 높다' 같은 긍정적인 말과 함께 나와요. '훨씬'은 어디에나 쓰지만 '월등히'는 비교하며 평가할 때 더 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 실력이 월등히 앞서 있어요.
phrases.en: That team is far ahead in skill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이나 팀보다 한참 앞선다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being well ahead of others.

phrases.en: This school's pass rate is far higher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비교했을 때 수치가 크게 높을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a figure is much higher in comparison.

phrases.en: This computer's performance is outstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '월등히'의 형용사 꼴로 문장을 끝낼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form that can end a sentence.

explain_en: Adverb for being far ahead in comparison (월등히 뛰어나다) It is similar to '훨씬' (much more), but strongly suggests being far ahead of or better than others in a comparison. It usually comes with positive words like '좋다', '뛰어나다', '앞서다' and '높다'. While '훨씬' fits anywhere, '월등히' suits evaluating things by comparison.

t90.ax: This product is far better than the others.

en: to be dense; to be densely built

examples.ko: 이 도시는 건물이 조밀해서 길이 좁아요.
examples.en: This city has densely packed buildings, so the roads are narrow.
The more densely populated the area, the higher the housing prices.
The trees in the forest are dense and tall, so it is dark.
If the net's mesh is fine, even small fish get caught.

examples.ko: 일정이 조밀하게 짜여 있어서 쉴 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: The schedule is packed so tightly that there is no time to rest.
The tighter the weave, the sturdier the fabric.

explain: '빽빽하다'와 비슷하지만 글이나 설명에서 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '성기다'이고, 작은 것들이 짜임새 있게 모인 느낌은 '오밀조밀하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 집이 많은 조밀한 지역에는 주차장이 부족해요.
phrases.en: Dense areas with many houses lack parking lots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form before a noun.

phrases.en: Small houses are densely packed together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조밀하게'로 모여 있는 모양을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '조밀하게' describes how things are gathered.

phrases.en: The houses in this village are not dense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 빽빽하지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning not crowded together.

explain_en: Dense — formal, packed population or buildings, written style (이 도시는 건물이 너무 조밀해서 걷기가 조금 답답해요.) It is close to '빽빽하다' but fits writing and explanations better. The opposite is '성기다', and for small things neatly gathered together you say '오밀조밀하다'.

t90.ax: The tighter the weave, the sturdier the fabric.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 중량이 5킬로그램이나 돼서 들기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This bag weighs as much as five kilograms, so it is hard to carry.

examples.ko: 비행기에 실을 수 있는 짐의 중량은 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The weight of baggage you can load on a plane is fixed.
The truck was overweight and got caught in a check.

examples.ko: 역도 선수는 바벨의 중량을 조금씩 올려요.
examples.en: A weightlifter raises the weight of the barbell little by little.
This bridge has a ten-ton weight limit.
This laptop weighs only one kilogram.

explain: '무게'는 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '중량'은 짐, 화물, 기계, 역도처럼 숫자로 정확히 재는 상황에서 더 자주 써요. 사람의 몸무게는 '중량'이라고 하지 않고 '체중'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This elevator has a weight limit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실을 수 있는 무게의 한계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the maximum weight something can carry.

phrases.en: I measured the weight of the luggage with a scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자로 정확히 무게를 잴 때 어울리는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits situations where weight is measured precisely in numbers.

phrases.en: How much does this box weigh?
phrases.nuance_ko: '중량'보다 일상에서 두루 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used more broadly in daily life than 중량.

explain_en: Formal or technical weight, as on labels (가방의 중량) 무게 is the everyday word, while 중량 is used more where weight is measured exactly, like cargo, machines and weightlifting. A person's body weight is 체중, not 중량.

t90.ax: This laptop weighs only one kilogram.

examples.ko: 아침 출근 시간이 지하철 이용객의 피크예요.
examples.en: The morning commute is the peak for subway riders.

examples.ko: 전기 사용량이 여름 오후에 피크를 찍었어요.
examples.en: Electricity use hit its peak on a summer afternoon.

examples.ko: 피크 시간을 피해서 가면 덜 막혀요.
examples.en: If you go avoiding peak hours, there is less traffic.

examples.ko: 감기 환자가 이번 주에 피크라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the number of cold patients is at its peak this week.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 인기는 이십 대에 피크였어요.
examples.en: That singer's popularity peaked in her twenties.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 점심 피크 때 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: This restaurant has a long line at the lunch peak.

explain: '피크 시간', '피크 타임'처럼 가장 붐비거나 가장 많은 때를 말할 때 써요. 산꼭대기라는 뜻으로는 잘 안 쓰고 '정상'이라고 해요. '절정'은 감정이나 분위기가 가장 높을 때 써서 조금 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: The subway is very crowded during peak hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 사용량이 가장 많은 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the time when people or usage are at their highest.

phrases.example: 전기 사용량이 여름 오후에 피크를 찍었어요.
phrases.en: Electricity use hit its peak on summer afternoons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자나 양이 가장 높은 지점에 닿았다는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a number or amount reached its highest point; common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 더위가 피크를 지나서 이제 조금 시원해요.
phrases.en: The heat has passed its peak, so it's a bit cooler now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 높은 때가 끝났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the highest point has passed.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like 피크 시간 and 피크 타임 for the busiest or highest-volume moment. For a mountain top, Koreans say 정상 instead. 절정 is for the high point of feelings or atmosphere, so the feel differs a little.

en: to be marked; to be significant; to be considerable

examples.en: The skill gap between the two teams is huge.

examples.ko: 도시와 시골의 소득 격차가 현격하게 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: The income gap between city and countryside has widened considerably.
Our goal is to reduce the large difference.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 기술 수준은 그렇게 현격하지 않아요.
examples.en: The technology levels of the two countries are not that far apart.
The temperature people felt differed greatly from person to person.

examples.ko: 결과가 현격하게 달라서 다시 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: The results were so different that I checked again.

explain: '차이', '격차', '간격' 같은 말 앞에서 자주 나와요. 둘을 비교해서 많이 다르다고 할 때 쓰는 글말 느낌의 표현이에요. 말할 때는 '차이가 엄청나요'처럼 더 쉽게 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 나라의 물가는 현격한 차이가 나요.
phrases.en: There is a marked difference in prices between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '차이'를 꾸밀 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use is before the noun 'difference'.

phrases.en: Life is considerably different now from before.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형 '현격하게'는 '다르다', '벌어지다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form goes well with 'differ' and 'widen'.

phrases.example: 두 제품의 품질 차이는 현격하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The quality difference between the two products is not significant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 차이가 크지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the difference is not large.

explain_en: It often appears before words like '차이', '격차', and '간격'. It is a somewhat written-style word used when comparing two things that differ a lot. In speech people often say something simpler like '차이가 엄청나요'.

examples.en: The supermarket is discounting processed meat products.
They're processed, so they last longer than fresh ones.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 수산물 가공품도 같이 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop also sells processed seafood products.

examples.ko: 아이에게는 가공품보다 신선한 과일을 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give my child fresh fruit rather than processed food.
I check the ingredients of processed goods on the packaging.

examples.ko: 농산물 가공품 수출이 늘었다는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that exports of processed farm products have grown.

explain: 원래 재료를 손질하거나 만들어 바꾼 물건이에요. 식품에서는 '가공식품'과 함께 많이 쓰고, 반대로 가공하지 않은 것은 '원재료'나 '생것'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: With processed food, it's easy to eat too much salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 것에 한해서 '가공품' 대신 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is widely used instead of 가공품 when talking about food only.

phrases.en: We make and sell processed farm products.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농산물, 수산물' 같은 말 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It follows words like 농산물 or 수산물.

phrases.en: They process fish to make fish cakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가공품'을 만드는 일을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb for making a 가공품.

explain_en: Broader: any goods made from raw materials, not only food (농산물 가공품) It refers to goods made by treating or transforming raw materials. For food it appears together with '가공식품', and unprocessed things are called '원재료' or '생것'.

en: to be alleviated; to be reduced

examples.en: The pain eased after I took the medicine.

examples.ko: 새 제도 덕분에 부담이 많이 경감돼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new system, the burden is eased a lot.

examples.ko: 세금이 경감되면 생활이 조금 나아질 거예요.
examples.en: If taxes are reduced, life will get a little better.
The doctor said the symptoms have eased.
With less homework, I feel my stress easing.
I'm checking whether the cost will go down.

explain: 덜어지는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요. '부담이 경감되다'처럼 말하고, 하는 사람을 말하려면 '경감하다'를 써요. '줄어들다'보다 딱딱하고 좋은 방향의 변화에 어울려요.

phrases.en: After taking medicine, the pain lessened a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경감되다'와 비슷하지만 더 부드럽고, 일상 대화에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 경감되다 but softer and comfortable to use in daily conversation.

phrases.example: 새 제도 덕분에 학부모의 부담이 경감됐어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the new system, parents' burden has been eased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 무거운 부담이 덜어진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; it means a heavy burden is lightened.
phrases.en_equiv: for a burden to be eased

phrases.en: I took medicine, but the pain wasn't relieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대한 만큼 덜어지지 않았을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used when something was not eased as much as expected.

explain_en: This is the side of the thing being eased. You say '부담이 경감되다'; to name who does the easing, use 경감하다. It is stiffer than 줄어들다 and fits changes for the better.

en: to be supplied; to be provided

examples.en: Electricity is supplied to every house.
The water was cut off and wasn't supplied.
Fresh vegetables are supplied to the shop every day.

examples.ko: 부품이 제때 공급되면 공장이 계속 돌아가요.
examples.en: If parts are supplied on time, the factory keeps running.
Here there are drinks supplied for free.
The amount supplied fell short, so the price went up.

explain: 전기·물·가스처럼 생활에 필요한 것이 필요한 곳으로 들어오는 상황에 자주 써요. 주는 쪽은 '공급하다'이고, 받는 쪽 입장에서는 '공급받다'예요. 경제에서는 '수요'와 짝이 되어 '수요와 공급'으로 나와요.

phrases.en: Our village gets its water supplied from the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 쪽 입장에서 말할 때 써요. '공급되다'와 거의 같은 상황이지만 받는 사람이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the receiver's side; the receiver is the subject, unlike 공급되다.

phrases.en: The electricity supply was cut off because of the typhoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공급되던 것이 갑자기 멈췄을 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for when a supply suddenly stops.

phrases.en: Fresh vegetables are being supplied every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 들어오는 중이라는 진행의 느낌을 더한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds an ongoing feeling: the supply keeps arriving.

explain_en: Passive: goods, water, power are provided to a place. It is common for utilities like electricity, water and gas reaching where they are needed. The giver's verb is 공급하다 and the receiver's is 공급받다. In economics it pairs with 수요 as '수요와 공급' (supply and demand).

examples.ko: 집을 고치는 데 공사비가 생각보다 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The construction cost for fixing the house was higher than I expected.
I chose cheap materials to cut construction costs.
I heard the city pays the construction cost of the new road.
The building plan was delayed because of construction costs.
The construction cost is written in detail in the estimate.

examples.ko: 가게를 열기 전에 공사비부터 계산해 봤어요.
examples.en: Before opening the shop, I first calculated the construction cost.

explain: '공사비'는 '공사'와 '비(돈)'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '건축비', '인테리어 비용'이 있어요. 집이나 길을 짓거나 고치는 일에 드는 돈에 두루 써요. '공사비가 들다', '공사비를 아끼다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The material prices went up, so the construction cost went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 더 필요해질 때 '오르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '오르다' when the cost rises.

phrases.en: I pay the construction cost when the work is finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 낼 때 '내다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '내다' when paying money.

phrases.en: Building costs went up, so house prices went up too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 건물을 지을 때 드는 돈에 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for the money needed to build a house or building.

explain_en: 공사비 combines 공사 (construction work) and 비 (cost). Similar words are 건축비 and 인테리어 비용. It is used broadly for money spent on building or repairing houses and roads. Common patterns are 공사비가 들다 and 공사비를 아끼다.

en: to tax; to impose a tax

examples.en: The state taxes differently depending on income.
Is value-added tax applied to this product too?
They started taxing rental income too.

examples.ko: 정부가 설탕이 든 음료에 과세하겠다고 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced it would tax sugary drinks.

examples.ko: 해외에서 번 돈에도 과세할 수 있어요.
examples.en: They can tax money earned abroad too.
Please explain on what basis they impose the tax.

explain: 말로는 '세금을 매기다'라고 많이 하고, '과세하다'는 뉴스·법·회계에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 반대로 세금을 안 매기는 것은 '면세하다'나 '비과세'라고 해요. '~에 과세하다'처럼 세금이 붙는 대상에 조사 '에'를 써요.

phrases.en: This income is taxed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금이 매겨지는 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, said from the side of what gets taxed.

phrases.en: The government imposed a tax on the new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '과세하다'를 쉽게 말한 표현이라 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say 과세하다, more natural in conversation.

phrases.en: This gift is not subject to tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금이 붙는 대상을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what is subject to taxation.

explain_en: In speech people often say '세금을 매기다'; '과세하다' is the stiff word used in news, law and accounting. The opposites are '면세하다' and '비과세' (no tax). The thing being taxed takes the particle '에', as in '~에 과세하다'.

en: advertising expense; advertising cost; advertising fee

examples.en: This month only the advertising cost went up a lot.
A new product came out, so we spent a lot on advertising.
We postponed making the video because the ad budget fell short.
Small shops feel the burden of advertising costs heavily.
How much did advertising cost this month?
The effect is small compared to the advertising cost.

phrases.en: It's a new product, so advertising costs a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 필요할 때 '들다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 들다 when money is needed.

phrases.en: I promote it myself to save on advertising costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용을 줄이려고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when trying to cut costs.

phrases.example: 가게 광고비를 한 달에 한 번 내요.
phrases.en: I pay the shop's advertising fee once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불할 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest collocation for paying money.

explain_en: It is used as '광고비를 쓰다/들이다/아끼다'. Other '-비' (cost) words include '교통비' and '식비'.
